industry.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 (Jefferies, 22 Oct), oil above $100 and rising, and energy led the week; energy is the hedge inside a European book against the shock that hurts everything else. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior at industry level. Not Double Overweight at the industry because the industry holds Metals and mining (relative strength F now from A) and Agriculture beside the three energy sectors; Downstream distribution carries the A. Counter-case: Goldman attributes part of the oil move to restocking, two months into leadership is where reversals begin, and 13 of the 18 upstream Pool names read F on TSR/Valuation, so the market has paid.

No memo carried a congruence line this week. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior. Counter-case: Goldman reads restocking into the oil move, and a European book with no energy at all (component 5) is the one that most needs this row to be right; back to C if Brent falls under $85.

memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the shares at EUR 21.97 (2026-10-01) and bearish relative to the sell-side's Overweight consensus; conviction medium, because the return arithmetic is clear and the commodity call that could overturn it is not ours to make. The gate line does not trigger: management ('No mediocre management') C, business quality ('Business') C, predictability ('Transmission') C, trackability ('Leading indicators') B. The park rests on the 'Modal return' at F (-6.3 percent a year over eighteen months; -0.3 percent a year over three years against a 20 percent-a-year bar) and 'Riskiness' at D. Re-open triggers: a price near EUR 15 (the eighteen-month entry level on the modal path; about EUR 13.7 on the worse drop-through); a first Mopane appraisal well confirming liquids with a manageable gas-oil ratio, bringing an FPSO concept and a 2027 FID; a signed Moeve agreement with a stated distribution; FY2027 consensus EPS above EUR 2.2 on a crack the market accepts as structural. The record's one-line bet it declines: that a company turning itself into a holder of stakes it does not operate keeps a refining windfall it does not control and earns, before 2028, a re-rating for Namibian oil it will not produce before 2032, at a price that already pays for both.
case: - The thesis: Galp is a self-help and portfolio-reshaping case riding a commodity peak, not a demand inflection and not a recovery. The internal change is broad, mostly completed and visible along the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain, but the earnings it has produced belong mostly to a refining margin the company does not set, and at EUR 21.97 the shares already pay for the peak year and for Namibian oil that will not flow before 2032.

- The internal change, inside twenty months: Filipe Silva resigned January 2025 after breaching internal rules on an undisclosed relationship with a direct report; Maria João Carioca (also CFO) and João Marques da Silva appointed co-chief executives April 2025, "for the remainder of the current mandate ending in 2026", a model management calls "highly unconventional"; the third departure since 2021 against a peer median of one. Strategy reset to "value over volume", renewables declared complete with "no further acquisition targets". Angola exited for USD 830 million (2024); Mozambique Area 4 sold for USD 881 million cash plus USD 100 million and USD 400 million contingent (March 2025); 40 percent of PEL 83 (Mopane) farmed down to TotalEnergies for a 50 percent capex carry to first oil (repaid from 50 percent of Galp's project cash flows), 10 percent of Venus and 9.39 percent of PEL 91, completed 3 September 2026; Bacalhau first oil October 2025 (Equinor-operated; 20 percent; 40 thousand barrels a day net at plateau from late 2026; breakeven near USD 20; early-life cash tax 15 to 30 percent); Moeve downstream combination (50/50 RetailCo; IndustrialCo minority above 20 percent) slipped from mid-2026 to the second half; 712 MW of Spanish onshore wind bought for EUR 738 million at about 10 percent unlevered; Aurora lithium and Northvolt cancelled; EUR 430 million of EIB debt for Sines projects.

- The screen passes on both limbs: five forces strong (strategy B, guidance B, perimeter B, shareholder returns B, Bacalhau delivery B) and chief-executive change C plus guidance increase B. False-positive flags: caretaker partly (mandate ends 2026); core-asset sale arguable (Mozambique; PEL 83 for no cash); the guidance rise commodity-driven in cause. 'Change Forces' B; 'Internal forces' B; 'External forces' C (refining tailwind without visibility; oil price without visibility; fiscal headwind intensifying, D; Iberian retail headwind; none meets the 'Demand Inflection' test).
counter_case: - At its strongest, Morgan Stanley's "Why We Remain Overweight" (07 September 2026) and its Defence Playbook (02 July 2026): Galp is the cleanest defensive compounder of cash among the European mid-majors. Gearing falls to 19 percent by 2027; the free cash flow yield is about 9 percent for 2026-27; the dividend can grow about 7.5 percent a year to the late 2030s; capex is a third of Repsol's; a sub-USD 20 breakeven makes the payout safe at USD 50 Brent; it holds a 40 percent stake in a 10 billion barrels-in-place discovery whose development is half paid for by the operator; and two value crystallisations (Moeve, EUR 1.2 billion; renewables, EUR 2.5 billion) would each be worth 7 to 15 percent of the market capitalisation. A stock like that should not trade at the European integrateds' 8 to 10 times, and 12 times is the right price for it. The evidence for it is the balance sheet at 0.40 times, the EUR 0.70 dividend floor, the three-year guidance record, the partner quality of TotalEnergies, Equinor and Petrobras, and the Bacalhau volumes, all of which the record rates at B or A where the framework asks about them.

- The record concedes: the downside in the corporate sense is bounded by those things; the shares are at their ten-year median and not at a mania level; and if the dividend truly compounds at 7.5 percent a year from a 3.2 percent yield the stock is a reasonable long-term holding.
triggers: - The commodity deck through 2027: plausible that the second half of 2026 beats the company's deck (Brent USD 70; refining USD 10); unlikely that 2027 and 2028 hold at 2026 levels. Changes the view: FY2027 consensus EPS rising above EUR 2.2 (from 1.94) on cracks structurally above USD 12, with the third-quarter print on 2026-10-26 showing a realised margin above the USD 13 full-year assumption.

- The Mopane appraisal (4Q26 through 2027): condition one, commercial liquids with a manageable gas-oil ratio by end-2027, probable at 60 percent (against: the gas-oil-ratio risk from the Kudu shale source, the swap's implied value of USD 1.7 billion below consensus on Jefferies, TotalEnergies' Venus-first sequencing); condition two, a re-rating to about 13.5 times given success, plausible at 50 percent; the re-rating branch 0.30, the disappointment branch 0.40. Changes the view: fluid samples from the first well showing high liquid recovery and a gas-oil ratio the operator calls manageable, with an FPSO concept and a 2027 FID rather than 2028.

- The Moeve combination: probable at 65 percent that definitive agreements sign between H2 2026 and H1 2027; possible at 40 percent given signing that an extraordinary distribution of about EUR 1.2 billion (7.7 percent of the market capitalisation) follows inside eighteen months; the branch 0.26, not in the modal path (against: Portuguese sovereignty caution on Sines; RetailCo leverage of 3 to 4 times still under due diligence). Changes the view: a signed agreement with a stated distribution.

- Bacalhau's plateau against Tupi's decline: probable at 70 percent that 2027 production holds at or above 135 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day. Changes the view the other way: a quarterly print below 125 thousand after plateau, or the ANP refusing the Tupi extension.

- The leadership after the 2026 mandate: plausible that the board confirms the pair or names a sole chief executive; possible that a fourth change in six years follows and reopens the "no chief executive" concern during the appraisal. Changes the view: a permanent single appointment with an operating background, or open-market buying by the executive board.

- The price: the case clears the bar on the modal path below EUR 15.2 (eighteen months) and EUR 12.6 (three years); about EUR 13.7 on the worse drop-through; the eighteen-month figure sits near Redburn's EUR 15.80 and Jefferies' January 2026 EUR 15.
